newsitem.title: FRANCE: French business activity seen expanding more - BoF.
newsitem.headline: French business activity seen expanding more - BoF.

text.p: French industrial activity continued to increase in most sectors in March and is set to keep expanding in the coming months, except in the automobile sector, the Bank of France said on Tuesday.
The central bank said in its monthly business survey in March: "In the coming months, activity should continue to increase, except in the automobile sector, where a further decline is forecast".

"Investment programmes for 1997 are getting underway in large companies, whereas small and medium-sized firms continue to be cautious," it said. "The investments carried out remain limited in scope and mainly concern the renewal or modernisation of existing equipment."
It said that March retail sales posted a "moderate rise" and that building industry activity had recovered after being hit by unfavourable weather at the start of the year.
The bank also highlighted that foreign demand for French products was strong but that the picture was less certain for domestic demand.
"Overall demand remained firm on the whole. there was strong demand for French products from North America, Asia and southern and eastern Europe. The domestic market seemed less certain," it said.

The survey said inventories of finished products were still above normal levels, "particularly in the automobile and consumer goods industries". "They are deemed to be normal in the capital goods sector," it added.
It said commodity price rises which had resulted from dollar appreciation had not fed through to final product prices because of intense competition.
